**Korean‑Content Localization & Marketing Playbook (2026 – Limited‑Budget Edition)** --- ## 1. Strategic Goal > **Turn the fast‑growing Korean‑content slate into a “regional growth engine” while spending ≈ $30 M on localization (dub + sub + marketing) and keeping the unit‑economics of each market inside the 66 % gross‑margin envelope defined in the Global Pricing Playbook.** The plan works **hand‑in‑hand** with the USD‑reference pricing model (Section 3 of the Local‑Pricing Playbook) – every extra dubbing or marketing cost is added as a **local‑cost line‑item**, then absorbed by the locally‑adjusted multiplier. --- ## 2. Regional Landscape – What Drives Localization Choices | Region / Country Cluster | Primary Language(s) | Sub‑vs‑Dub Preference (share of total Korean‑content consumption) | Sensitivity to Adaptation (historical / cultural) | Typical Dub‑Studio Cost (USD / hour) | Fandom‑Community Dynamics | |--------------------------|----------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------|---------------------------| | **Southeast Asia**
(Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam) | Bahasa Ind, Malay, Tagalog, Thai, Vietnamese | 70 % Sub, 30 % Dub (high for kids & action‑drama) | Medium – strong reaction to Korean‑Japan historical references; modest to Korean‑China. | $80 – $120 (Vietnam & Thailand cheaper) | Highly active Discord / TikTok fan hubs; fan‑sub groups still strong. | | **Middle East & North‑Africa (MENA)**
(UAE, Saudi, Egypt, Morocco) | Arabic (MSA + local dialects) | 45 % Sub, 55 % Dub (preference for full‑audio in households) | High – any depiction of the “Korean‑Japanese” wartime era triggers political backlash; modest about Korean‑Chinese. | $150 – $200 (high‑quality MSA) | Fan pages on Instagram & Facebook; “watch‑parties” organised via local influencers. | | **Latin America**
(Brazil, Mexico, Colombia, Argentina, Chile) | Portuguese (BR) & Spanish (LatAm) | 55 % Sub, 45 % Dub (dub strongest in Brazil and kids‑content) | Medium‑High – strong pride in local historical narratives; dislikes “political” Korean‑Japan references. | $100 – $130 (Brazil higher) | Massive fan‑translation movement on YouTube; fandom “cosplay” communities on TikTok. | | **Europe (Western)**
(France, Germany, Italy, Spain, UK) | French, German, Italian, Spanish, English | 80 % Sub, 20 % Dub (dub only for family/children) | Low‑Medium – limited political sensitivity; more focus on cultural authenticity (e.g., proper Korean food/ customs). | $120 – $170 (German, French premium) | Highly organized fan‑clubs on Reddit & Discord; “voting” for dub releases is common. | | **Europe (Eastern)**
(Poland, Czech, Hungary, Russia, Ukraine) | Polish, Czech, Hungarian, Russian | 65 % Sub, 35 % Dub (dub for blockbuster‑type K‑dramas) | Medium – some historical friction with Japanese WWII content; high demand for “clean” versions. | $90 – $130 (Russia cheaper) | Fandoms thrive on “fan‑edits” and subtitles; expect community‑led promotion. | > **Key Insight:** > *Subtitles are the cheapest way to cover the entire slate, but dubbing drives the biggest lift in ARPU for family‑share and kids‑segments and is mandatory in markets where auto‑renewal payments are tied to “full‑audio” purchases (MENA, Brazil).* --- ## 3. Budget Allocation Framework ### 3.1. Total Localization Budget | Line‑Item | Amount (USD) | % of Total | |-----------|--------------|------------| | **Voice‑Dub Production** | $18 M | 60 % | | **Subtitle Production & QC** | $4 M | 13 % | | **Cultural‑Clearance & Adaptation (script‑review, legal, sensitivity consulting)** | $2 M | 7 % | | **Fan‑Community Seeding (micro‑grants, co‑creation, UGC contests)** | $3 M | 10 % | | **Targeted Marketing (language‑specific paid media, influencer bundles, OTT‑bundle discounts)** | $5 M | 17 % | | **Contingency / Pilot Experiments** | $1 M | 3 % | | **TOTAL** | **$30 M** | **100 %** | > The split reflects the **highest ROI activity**: **dub where it unlocks premium pricing or family‑share uptake** (MENA & Brazil), **subtitles everywhere**, and **community‑driven marketing** that can amplify limited spend. ### 3.2. How Dollars Translate to Episodes Assume an **average Korean drama** = 16 episodes × ≈ 1 hour each. | Market Cluster | Avg. Dub Cost per Episode (USD) | Avg. Sub Cost per Episode (USD) | Episodes Covered with $18 M Dub Budget | |----------------|--------------------------------|---------------------------------|----------------------------------------| | **Southeast Asia (average)** | $100 × 1 hr = $100 | $12 × 1 hr = $12 | 180 episodes (≈ 11 dramas) | | **MENA (Arabic MSA)** | $180 × 1 hr = $180 | $12 | 100 episodes (≈ 6 dramas) | | **LatAm (Spanish/Portuguese)** | $115 × 1 hr = $115 | $12 | 156 episodes (≈ 10 dramas) | | **Western Europe** | $145 × 1 hr = $145 | $12 | 124 episodes (≈ 8 dramas) | | **Eastern Europe** | $110 × 1 hr = $110 | $12 | 164 episodes (≈ 11 dramas) | **Practical outcome:** *We can fully dub **5‑8 flagship titles** (high‑potential dramas & action‑packed series) across the regions that need dub the most, while providing **sub‑only** for the remaining slate.* --- ## 4. Prioritisation Matrix – Which Title Gets Dub Where? | Rank | Title (genre) | Global “Growth Potential” Score* | Dub Needed In | Sub‑Only In | Rationale | |------|---------------|----------------------------------|--------------|------------|-----------| | 1 | **“Moonlit Warrior”** (Historical action) | 9.2 | MENA, Brazil, Indonesia, Thailand | All other markets | High‑action → dub needed for family/young viewers; historical content → need cultural‑clearance; strong fandom traction in Brazil & MENA. | | 2 | **“Seoul Café”** (Rom‑com) | 8.7 | Brazil, Mexico, Philippines | Rest of SEA, EU, MENA | Romantic comedy is subtitle‑friendly but Brazil’s “family‑share” model prefers dub for multitasking households. | | 3 | **“Neon High”** (Teen‑drama) | 8.3 | Indonesia, Philippines, Saudi Arabia | EU, LATAM, Eastern EU | Teen audience cares more about dub (easier for younger kids). | | 4 | **“Ghost of Han River”** (Supernatural thriller) | 7.9 | Turkey (MENA‑ish), Poland, Germany | Rest | Supernatural genre benefits from dub for immersion; fan‑sub community already strong in EU. | | 5 | **“Dreamscape”** (Sci‑fi anthology) | 7.5 | Vietnam, Malaysia, Argentina | Rest | Sci‑fi fans often prefer subtitle for technical jargon; dub only where OTT bundle promotions target families. | | 6‑10 | Remaining 5‑10 titles (varied) | 6‑7 | Sub‑only everywhere, selective dub (pilot test) | — | Use these as **test‑beds** for community‑driven dub experiments (see §7). | \*Score = weighted sum of (historical ARPU uplift, social‑buzz potential, genre‑dub‑need, regional fan‑size). --- ## 5. Localization Production Workflow ### 5.1. Central “K‑Content Hub” (HQ – Seoul) | Function | Tool | Deliverable | Turn‑around | |----------|------|-------------|-------------| | **Script Extraction & Translation** | SDL Trados, Memsource, internal Korean‑to‑English master | Master English script (time‑coded) | 2 days per 10‑min segment | | **Subtitle Creation** | Subtitle Edit + AI‑assist (DeepL, Google Gemini) | SRT / VTT files (English → Local language) | 3 days per episode | | **Cultural‑Clearance Review** | Local cultural consultants (contracted per region) | “Clearance Flags” (historical, religious, political) | 1 day per episode | | **Dub Production Pack** | Exported .xml + Audio‑track file | Voice‑over script, cue sheet | 1 day | ### 5.2. Regional “Dub‑Partner Network” | Region | Preferred Partner(s) | Contract Model | Cost‑Control Mechanism | |--------|----------------------|----------------|------------------------| | **Southeast Asia** | **Vocaloid Studios** (Indonesia), **Lyric Studios** (Thailand) | Fixed‑price per hour + **quality‑gate KPI** (DSP ≥ 85) | Milestone payments + 5 % penalty for missed quality. | | **MENA** | **MBC Media**, **Arab Voice** (Dubai) | Revenue‑share (5 % of incremental ARPU) + base cost $150/hr | Guarantees ROI; if ARPU lift < 3 % after 3 months, re‑negotiate. | | **LatAm** | **Grupo Globo Audio**, **Vox Studios** (Mexico) | Fixed price per minute + **dial‑in** for accent‑regionalization | Use “voice‑type template” to reuse the same actor across Spanish‑LATAM, saving 12 % per episode. | | **Western Europe** | **Studio Babel**, **Dubbing Brothers** (Paris, Berlin) | Fixed per hour, discount for batch‑booking (≥ 3 titles) | Audits every 6 months; replace partner if average DSP < 80. | | **Eastern Europe** | **Mediaplex**, **Kultura Voice** (Warsaw, Moscow) | Fixed + “local‑dialect” add‑on | Tiered pricing: standard Russian dub $110/hr, dialect‑specific $130/hr. | > **Quality Gate:** All dubs must meet **DSP (Dub Speech‑Quality) ≥ 85** (measured by independent VCT‑Score) and **Lip‑Sync Error ≤ 0.5 s**. --- ## 6. Cultural‑Sensitivity & Adaptation Process 1. **Pre‑Production “Historical Lens” Review** – Cultural‑consultant delivers a **“Red‑Flag Matrix”** (e.g., any mention of 1905‑1910 Japanese occupation). 2. **Localized “Edit‑Option Library”** – For each flagged line, the hub stores three options: * *Original* (kept for markets with low sensitivity). * *Neutral* (re‑worded to remove reference). * *Explainer‑Subtitle* (adds a short footnote in the subtitle). 3. **Decision Engine (Rule‑Based)** – * If market = MENA OR LATAM AND red‑flag = Korean‑Japan ⇒ use *Neutral* in dub & subtitle. * If market = EU OR SEA AND red‑flag = Korean‑China ⇒ keep *Original* (lower sensitivity). 4. **Community‑Feedback Loop** – After launch, the **Fandom‑Insight Team** monitors Twitter/Reddit for “cultural‑error” spikes; any validated issue triggers a **quick‑fix patch** (sub update, dub re‑recording) within **48 h**. --- ## 7. Fandom‑Centric Marketing – “Community‑First” Spend | Tactic | Target Region | Execution Details | Cost (USD) | Expected Lift (ARPU / Subs) | |--------|---------------|-------------------|------------|-----------------------------| | **Localized “Watch‑Party” Livestream** (hosted by top K‑drama fan‑page) | SEA, LATAM | 2‑hour live chat with subtitles on, local influencer invites fans. | $300 k (production + influencer fees) | +6 % week‑on‑week new subs in that region | | **UGC Dub Contest** (fans submit their own voice‑over for a 1‑min teaser) | MENA, Brazil | Winner’s voice used in official promo; prize = 1‑yr premium + cash. | $400 k (prize + platform cost) | +4 % conversion from “teaser viewers” | | **“Behind‑the‑Scenes Korean Culture” Mini‑Docs** (localized subtitles only) | EU, SE Asia | 5‑min doc per title, released on YouTube & in‑app “Explore” section. | $500 k (production + translation) | Improves “cultural affinity” score; reduces churn by 2 % | | **Micro‑Grants for Fan‑Translation Communities** | All regions | $50 k per region to support existing fan‑sub groups (software licensing, legal clearance). | $1.0 M | Generates goodwill; reduces pirated sub leakage by ~15 % | | **Localized Paid Media Bundles** (e.g., “Free 1‑month with local carrier” + Korean‑content carousel) | MENA (carrier‑billing), Brazil (telecom), Indonesia (GoPay) | Co‑marketing spend shared 60/40; assets include dub‑trailers where applicable. | $3.0 M | Direct acquisition CAC ↓ 20 % vs. generic OTT ads | | **Influencer “K‑Drama Challenge”** (TikTok dance/scene reenactment) | LATAM, SEA | 10‑K‑follower creators, localized hashtags. | $500 k | Social reach +8 M impressions; subs ↑ 1.8 % | **Total Community‑Marketing Spend:** **≈ $5 M** (fits the allocated $3 M for fan‑seeding + $2 M for targeted ads, with a small re‑allocation from “contingency”). --- ## 8. KPIs & Success Measurement | KPI | Target (12 mo) | How Measured | Frequency | |-----|----------------|--------------|-----------| | **Dub‑Driven ARPU Lift** (per market) | +12 % vs. sub‑only baseline | Revenue‑per‑user from dub‑enabled tiers (tracked via EMP) | Monthly | | **Subtitle‑Only Conversion Rate** | 5 % of impressions → paid subs | Funnel: Impressions → trial → paid (segmented by sub‑only) | Weekly | | **Cultural‑Error Incidents** | < 0.5 % of total episodes per market | Automated social‑listen sentiment + manual QC | Real‑time alert | | **Fan‑Engagement Index** (shares, comments, UGC submissions) | +30 % YoY | Platform analytics (in‑app + external socials) | Monthly | | **Cost‑per‑Dub‑Minute** | ≤ $0.14 USD | Total dubbing spend ÷ total dubbed minutes | Quarterly | | **Localization ROI** | ≥ 2.5 × (incremental revenue ÷ total spend) | Revenue uplift attributed to dub/marketing (incremental ARPU × new subs) | Quarterly | | **FX‑Adjusted Gross Margin** (post‑localization cost) | ≥ 66 % | Finance model that adds local costs to multiplier (see Section 3) | Monthly | > **Dashboard** – a single “K‑Content Localization Health” page feeds directly into the existing **Investor‑Relations KPI deck** (Section 10 of the Global Pricing Playbook) showing **EMP‑adjusted margin**, **FX‑adjustment**, and **local‑cost variance**. --- ## 9. Timeline – 18‑Month Roll‑out | Month | Milestone | Deliverable | |-------|-----------|-------------| | **M0‑M2** | **Foundational set‑up** | Sign dubbing‑partner contracts; hire regional cultural‑consultants; build “Red‑Flag Matrix”. | | **M3‑M5** | **Pilot Dub & Sub** (2 titles – “Moonlit Warrior”, “Seoul Café”) | Launch in MENA (dub), Brazil (dub), SEA (sub), EU (sub). Collect early KPI. | | **M6** | **First Community Campaign** – Watch‑Party in Indonesia + micro‑grant to fan‑sub community in Brazil. | | **M7‑M9** | **Expand Dub Coverage** – add 3 more titles (total 5) in high‑priority markets; begin “UGC Dub Contest”. | | **M10‑M12** | **Mid‑Year Review** – KPI audit; re‑allocate remaining dub budget based on ROI (e.g., shift extra dub hours from Latin America to MENA if needed). | | **M13‑M15** | **Full‑Scale Marketing Push** – carrier‑bundles, influencer challenges, localized paid‑media bundles. | | **M16‑M18** | **Optimization & Scaling** – introduce “dub‑reuse” across dialects (Spanish‑LATAM -> Mexican dubbing for other Latin markets), finalize all 10‑title slate. Prepare FY‑2027 budget recommendation. | --- ## 10. Risk Management | Risk | Probability | Impact | Mitigation | |------|-------------|--------|------------| | **FX spikes increase dub‑cost in local currency** | Medium | Margin compression | Hedge 75 % of projected local‑currency dub spend; embed FX‑buffer in multiplier (already in Pricing Playbook). | | **Cultural backlash on a historical reference** | Low‑Medium (MENA) | Reputation, temporary suspension | Pre‑clearance matrix + quick‑fix patch capability (48 h). | | **Dub‑partner quality falls short** | Medium | Fan‑complaints, churn | DSP ≥ 85 KPI + penalty clause; maintain “backup‑partner” pool in each region. | | **Fan‑sub community feels marginalized** | Medium | Piracy rise, brand‑harm | Micro‑grants, co‑creation contests, clear attribution of fan contributions. | | **Budget overrun on influencer bundles** | Low | Cash‑flow strain | Cap each campaign at a pre‑determined CPM; shift excess to paid‑media if KPI miss. | A **Monthly Risk‑Heat Map** is filed to the Global CFO and the **Global Localization Steering Committee** (GLSC) – a cross‑functional group (Product, Finance, Legal, Marketing, Regional Ops). --- ## 11. Executive Summary – “What to Do with $30 M” 1. **Allocate 60 % of the budget to dubbing** for the **5‑8 highest‑potential Korean titles** in markets where dub is a proven ARPU lever (MENA, Brazil, Indonesia, Saudi Arabia). 2. **Spend 13 % on subtitles** to guarantee **full‑catalog coverage** and keep acquisition cost low. 3. **Invest 7 % in cultural‑clearance** to avoid political backlash and preserve brand safety. 4. **Devote 10 % to fan‑centric programs** (micro‑grants, contests, community watch‑parties) that turn organic fandom into acquisition engines. 5. **Use the remaining 17 % for laser‑targeted paid media and carrier‑bundle deals** that link locally‑priced subscriptions (see Local‑Pricing Playbook) to the newly‑dubbed content. **Resulting Business Case (12‑month forecast):** | Region | Incremental Subs from K‑content | Incremental Revenue (USD) | Incremental Gross Margin (USD) | |--------|--------------------------------|---------------------------|--------------------------------| | **MENA** | +1.2 M | $12.9 M | $8.7 M | | **LATAM** | +1.5 M | $13.5 M | $9.0 M | | **SEA** | +2.0 M (sub‑only) | $9.2 M | $6.0 M | | **EU (Western)** | +0.8 M (sub‑only) | $5.6 M | $3.7 M | | **EU (Eastern)** | +0.9 M (mixed) | $6.4 M | $4.2 M | | **TOTAL** | **~6.4 M** | **$48 M** | **$31 M** | *Incremental margin includes the 66 % gross‑margin target; after deducting the $30 M localization spend, **EBITDA‑ex‑FX rises by ≈ $8 M**—a **27 % ROI** on the localization budget.* --- ## 12. Next Steps for the Board 1. **Approve the $30 M allocation** (with a 3‑month “pilot‑only” lock‑step). 2. **Mandate the formation of the Global Localization Steering Committee** (GLSC) – deliver the first KPI dashboard by **Month 4**. 3. **Authorize the first two pilot titles** (“Moonlit Warrior”, “Seoul Café”) with the pre‑approved dubbing partners. 4. **Kick‑off the “Fan‑Community Seeding” fund** – sign the micro‑grant agreements with the top 5 fan‑sub groups in each region. *Once the pilot data are in (Month 6), the GLSC will re‑balance the remaining $18 M of dub spend to the highest‑performing markets, ensuring the final 18‑month roll‑out delivers the **maximum ARPU lift per dollar spent** while keeping the consolidated unit‑economics comfortably within the 66 % margin envelope.* --- **Prepared by:** *Global Content Localization & Marketing Team* *Date: 23 August 2026*

run.userPrompt:
In 2026, a streaming platform's Korean-content slate is its fastest-growing category across Southeast Asia, the Middle East, Latin America, and Europe. Audiences differ in subtitle-versus-dubbing preferences, tolerance for adaptation edits, and sensitivity to historical and cultural references; dubbing-studio quality and costs vary widely by language, and fandom communities organize transnationally.

Design a localization and marketing strategy for Korean content across regions with different dubbing expectations, cultural sensitivities, and fandom dynamics, allocating a limited localization budget.

replace partner if average DSP < 80. | | **Eastern Europe** | **Mediaplex**, **Kultura Voice** (Warsaw, Moscow) | Fixed + “local‑dialect” add‑on | Tiered pricing: standard Russian dub $110/hr, dialect‑specific $130/hr. | > **Quality Gate:** All dubs must meet **DSP (Dub Speech‑Quality) ≥ 85** (measured by independent VCT‑Score) and **Lip‑Sync Error ≤ 0.5 s**. --- ## 6. Cultural‑Sensitivity & Adaptation Process 1. **Pre‑Production “Historical Lens” Review** – Cultural‑consultant delivers a **“Red‑Flag Matrix”** (e.g., any mention of 1905‑1910 Japanese occupation). 2. **Localized “Edit‑Option Library”** – For each flagged line, the hub stores three options: * *Original* (kept for markets with low sensitivity). * *Neutral* (re‑worded to remove reference). * *Explainer‑Subtitle* (adds a short footnote in the subtitle). 3. **Decision Engine (Rule‑Based)** – * If market = MENA OR LATAM AND red‑flag = Korean‑Japan ⇒ use *Neutral* in dub & subtitle. * If market = EU OR SEA AND red‑flag = Korean‑China ⇒ keep *Original* (lower sensitivity). 4. **Community‑Feedback Loop** – After launch, the **Fandom‑Insight Team** monitors Twitter/Reddit for “cultural‑error” spikes; any validated issue triggers a **quick‑fix patch** (sub update, dub re‑recording) within **48 h**. --- ## 7. Fandom‑Centric Marketing – “Community‑First” Spend | Tactic | Target Region | Execution Details | Cost (USD) | Expected Lift (ARPU / Subs) | |--------|---------------|-------------------|------------|-----------------------------| | **Localized “Watch‑Party” Livestream** (hosted by top K‑drama fan‑page) | SEA, LATAM | 2‑hour live chat with subtitles on, local influencer invites fans. | $300 k (production + influencer fees) | +6 % week‑on‑week new subs in that region | | **UGC Dub Contest** (fans submit their own voice‑over for a 1‑min teaser) | MENA, Brazil | Winner’s voice used in official promo; prize = 1‑yr premium + cash. | $400 k (prize + platform cost) | +4 % conversion from “teaser viewers” | | **“Behind‑the‑Scenes Korean Culture” Mini‑Docs** (localized subtitles only) | EU, SE Asia | 5‑min doc per title, released on YouTube & in‑app “Explore” section. | $500 k (production + translation) | Improves “cultural affinity” score; reduces churn by 2 % | | **Micro‑Grants for Fan‑Translation Communities** | All regions | $50 k per region to support existing fan‑sub groups (software licensing, legal clearance). | $1.0 M | Generates goodwill; reduces pirated sub leakage by ~15 % | | **Localized Paid Media Bundles** (e.g., “Free 1‑month with local carrier” + Korean‑content carousel) | MENA (carrier‑billing), Brazil (telecom), Indonesia (GoPay) | Co‑marketing spend shared 60/40; assets include dub‑trailers where applicable. | $3.0 M | Direct acquisition CAC ↓ 20 % vs. generic OTT ads | | **Influencer “K‑Drama Challenge”** (TikTok dance/scene reenactment) | LATAM, SEA | 10‑K‑follower creators, localized hashtags. | $500 k | Social reach +8 M impressions; subs ↑ 1.8 % | **Total Community‑Marketing Spend:** **≈ $5 M** (fits the allocated $3 M for fan‑seeding + $2 M for targeted ads, with a small re‑allocation from “contingency”). --- ## 8. KPIs & Success Measurement | KPI | Target (12 mo) | How Measured | Frequency | |-----|----------------|--------------|-----------| | **Dub‑Driven ARPU Lift** (per market) | +12 % vs. sub‑only baseline | Revenue‑per‑user from dub‑enabled tiers (tracked via EMP) | Monthly | | **Subtitle‑Only Conversion Rate** | 5 % of impressions → paid subs | Funnel: Impressions → trial → paid (segmented by sub‑only) | Weekly | | **Cultural‑Error Incidents** | < 0.5 % of total episodes per market | Automated social‑listen sentiment + manual QC | Real‑time alert | | **Fan‑Engagement Index** (shares, comments, UGC submissions) | +30 % YoY | Platform analytics (in‑app + external socials) | Monthly | | **Cost‑per‑Dub‑Minute** | ≤ $0.14 USD | Total dubbing spend ÷ total dubbed minutes | Quarterly | | **Localization ROI** | ≥ 2.5 × (incremental revenue ÷ total spend) | Revenue uplift attributed to dub/marketing (incremental ARPU × new subs) | Quarterly | | **FX‑Adjusted Gross Margin** (post‑localization cost) | ≥ 66 % | Finance model that adds local costs to multiplier (see Section 3) | Monthly | > **Dashboard** – a single “K‑Content Localization Health” page feeds directly into the existing **Investor‑Relations KPI deck** (Section 10 of the Global Pricing Playbook) showing **EMP‑adjusted margin**, **FX‑adjustment**, and **local‑cost variance**. --- ## 9. Timeline – 18‑Month Roll‑out | Month | Milestone | Deliverable | |-------|-----------|-------------| | **M0‑M2** | **Foundational set‑up** | Sign dubbing‑partner contracts; hire regional cultural‑consultants; build “Red‑Flag Matrix”. | | **M3‑M5** | **Pilot Dub & Sub** (2 titles – “Moonlit Warrior”, “Seoul Café”) | Launch in MENA (dub), Brazil (dub), SEA (sub), EU (sub). Collect early KPI. | | **M6** | **First Community Campaign** – Watch‑Party in Indonesia + micro‑grant to fan‑sub community in Brazil. | | **M7‑M9** | **Expand Dub Coverage** – add 3 more titles (total 5) in high‑priority markets; begin “UGC Dub Contest”. | | **M10‑M12** | **Mid‑Year Review** – KPI audit; re‑allocate remaining dub budget based on ROI (e.g., shift extra dub hours from Latin America to MENA if needed). | | **M13‑M15** | **Full‑Scale Marketing Push** – carrier‑bundles, influencer challenges, localized paid‑media bundles. | | **M16‑M18** | **Optimization & Scaling** – introduce “dub‑reuse” across dialects (Spanish‑LATAM -> Mexican dubbing for other Latin markets), finalize all 10‑title slate. Prepare FY‑2027 budget recommendation. | --- ## 10. Risk Management | Risk | Probability | Impact | Mitigation | |------|-------------|--------|------------| | **FX spikes increase dub‑cost in local currency** | Medium | Margin compression | Hedge 75 % of projected local‑currency dub spend; embed FX‑buffer in multiplier (already in Pricing Playbook). | | **Cultural backlash on a historical reference** | Low‑Medium (MENA) | Reputation, temporary suspension | Pre‑clearance matrix + quick‑fix patch capability (48 h). | | **Dub‑partner quality falls short** | Medium | Fan‑complaints, churn | DSP ≥ 85 KPI + penalty clause; maintain “backup‑partner” pool in each region. | | **Fan‑sub community feels marginalized** | Medium | Piracy rise, brand‑harm | Micro‑grants, co‑creation contests, clear attribution of fan contributions. | | **Budget overrun on influencer bundles** | Low | Cash‑flow strain | Cap each campaign at a pre‑determined CPM; shift excess to paid‑media if KPI miss. | A **Monthly Risk‑Heat Map** is filed to the Global CFO and the **Global Localization Steering Committee** (GLSC) – a cross‑functional group (Product, Finance, Legal, Marketing, Regional Ops). --- ## 11. Executive Summary – “What to Do with $30 M” 1. **Allocate 60 % of the budget to dubbing** for the **5‑8 highest‑potential Korean titles** in markets where dub is a proven ARPU lever (MENA, Brazil, Indonesia, Saudi Arabia). 2. **Spend 13 % on subtitles** to guarantee **full‑catalog coverage** and keep acquisition cost low. 3. **Invest 7 % in cultural‑clearance** to avoid political backlash and preserve brand safety. 4. **Devote 10 % to fan‑centric programs** (micro‑grants, contests, community watch‑parties) that turn organic fandom into acquisition engines. 5. **Use the remaining 17 % for laser‑targeted paid media and carrier‑bundle deals** that link locally‑priced subscriptions (see Local‑Pricing Playbook) to the newly‑dubbed content. **Resulting Business Case (12‑month forecast):** | Region | Incremental Subs from K‑content | Incremental Revenue (USD) | Incremental Gross Margin (USD) | |--------|--------------------------------|---------------------------|--------------------------------| | **MENA** | +1.2 M | $12.9 M | $8.7 M | | **LATAM** | +1.5 M | $13.5 M | $9.0 M | | **SEA** | +2.0 M (sub‑only) | $9.2 M | $6.0 M | | **EU (Western)** | +0.8 M (sub‑only) | $5.6 M | $3.7 M | | **EU (Eastern)** | +0.9 M (mixed) | $6.4 M | $4.2 M | | **TOTAL** | **~6.4 M** | **$48 M** | **$31 M** | *Incremental margin includes the 66 % gross‑margin target; after deducting the $30 M localization spend, **EBITDA‑ex‑FX rises by ≈ $8 M**—a **27 % ROI** on the localization budget.* --- ## 12. Next Steps for the Board 1. **Approve the $30 M allocation** (with a 3‑month “pilot‑only” lock‑step). 2. **Mandate the formation of the Global Localization Steering Committee** (GLSC) – deliver the first KPI dashboard by **Month 4**. 3. **Authorize the first two pilot titles** (“Moonlit Warrior”, “Seoul Café”) with the pre‑approved dubbing partners. 4. **Kick‑off the “Fan‑Community Seeding” fund** – sign the micro‑grant agreements with the top 5 fan‑sub groups in each region. *Once the pilot data are in (Month 6), the GLSC will re‑balance the remaining $18 M of dub spend to the highest‑performing markets, ensuring the final 18‑month roll‑out delivers the **maximum ARPU lift per dollar spent** while keeping the consolidated unit‑economics comfortably within the 66 % margin envelope.* --- **Prepared by:** *Global Content Localization & Marketing Team* *Date: 23 August 2026*
